questions.question: Solve: cos 2θ = cos θ
questions.solution:
cos 2θ = cos θ
2cos²θ - 1 = cos θ
2cos²θ - cos θ - 1 = 0
(2cos θ + 1)(cos θ - 1) = 0

Case 1: cos θ = 1 → θ = 0, 2π
Case 2: cos θ = -1/2 → θ = 2π/3, 4π/3

**Solutions: θ = 0, 2π/3, 4π/3, 2π**

questions.question: Solve for $x$, $0^{\circ}<x<90^{\circ}$: (i) $\displaystyle \frac{\sin x}{1+\cos x}+\frac{1+\cos x}{\sin x}=2\sqrt3$  (ii) $3\sin^{2}x-4\cos^{2}x+1=0$
questions.solution:
**(i)** Multiply the second numerator and denominator by $(1-\cos x)$:
$$\frac{\sin x}{1+\cos x}=\frac{\sin x(1-\cos x)}{1-\cos^{2}x}=\frac{\sin x(1-\cos x)}{\sin^{2}x}=\frac{1-\cos x}{\sin x}$$
So the left side becomes
$$\frac{1-\cos x}{\sin x}+\frac{1+\cos x}{\sin x}=\frac{2}{\sin x}$$
Hence $2\sin x = 2\sqrt3 \Rightarrow \sin x = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}$, giving
$$x=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt3}\right)\approx 35.264^{\circ}\approx\boxed{35^{\circ}16'\text{ (approximately)}}$$

**(ii)** Using $\sin^{2}x=1-\cos^{2}x$:
$$3(1-\cos^{2}x)-4\cos^{2}x+1=0$$
$$3-3\cos^{2}x-4\cos^{2}x+1=0\Longrightarrow 4-7\cos^{2}x=0$$
$$\cos x=\frac{2}{\sqrt7}\quad(\cos x>0\text{ on }0^{\circ}\!<x\!<90^{\circ})$$
$$x=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt7}\right)\approx\boxed{40.9^{\circ}}$$
questions.knowledgeNote: $\frac{\sin x}{1+\cos x}=\frac{1-\cos x}{\sin x}=\tan\frac{x}{2}$; their sum collapses to $\frac{2}{\sin x}$.
